preamble: Prothesis of the labio-velar glide [w] before a word-initial rounded back vowel. It is regular in Upper Sorbian, where Proto-Slavic word-initial *o and *u developed a prothetic [u̯] (written ⟨w⟩): *oko > woko 'eye', *uxo > wucho 'ear', *onъ > wón 'he'. As a result, native words in Upper Sorbian do not begin with o or u; initial [u, o] occur only in recent borrowings. Non-standard West Slavic dialects show the same glide, e.g. dialectal Polish [u̯oćec] 'father'. Prothetic /v/ in Ukrainian, Belarusian, Polish and Czech (vikno, wątroba, vokno) is a different outcome and belongs under empty → v.

examples.note: Upper Sorbian /w/ is a velarized bilabial approximant [β̞ˠ].

examples.from: Proto-Slavic *onъ 'he' (cf. Polish on); Proto-Slavic *orati 'to plough' (cf. Polish orać)
examples.note: The glide is regular before initial o and u. It also appears in prefixed words such as wobdarjować 'to reward' (cf. Polish obdarować).

sources: Bloch-Rozmej, A. (2018). Prosthetic consonants and the question of nuclear impact: Examples from Slavic languages. Roczniki Humanistyczne 66(11). https://doi.org/10.18290/rh.2018.66.11-2
